state.task: We have a Go microservice at `~/repos/api-gateway/` that proxies requests to about a dozen downstream services. Right now every upstream client can hammer any endpoint without limits and we've already had two outages from a single misbehaving partner flooding our `/transactions/bulk` endpoint. I need you to design and implement a robust rate limiting layer as middleware. Requirements: per-API-key limits with different tiers (free: 100 req/min, pro: 1000 req/min, enterprise: 10k req/min), a sliding window log algorithm for accuracy, a token bucket fallback for burst tolerance on the enterprise tier, and since we run 8 replicas behind an ALB, the counters need to be shared via our existing Redis Cluster (already configured in `config/redis.go`). Also, the rate limit headers (`X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `X-RateLimit-Reset`, `Retry-After`) need to be set on every response. When a client is throttled, return a `429` with a JSON body that includes how many seconds until their window resets. Finally, add a `/internal/rate-limits` admin endpoint that shows current consumption for all active API keys so our ops team can monitor abuse in real time. Can you scaffold this out with tests that simulate concurrent requests from multiple keys hitting the limits?
